title: How should the planner estimate walking time?
context: Hikers plan their day around the time estimate, not the distance. The planner shows a single figure today (distance divided by 4 km/h), which ignores climbing and is far off on steep routes.

options.name: Naismith's rule
options.summary: One hour per 5 km, plus one hour per 600 m of climbing.
options.sketch: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 180'><rect x='20' y='20' width='280' height='140' rx='6' fill='var(--muted)' fill-opacity='0.12'/><path d='M30 150 L90 150 L150 70 L210 70 L290 150' fill='none' stroke='currentColor' stroke-opacity='0.5' stroke-width='2'/><g stroke='var(--accent)' stroke-width='3' fill='none'><path d='M30 135 H90'/><path d='M90 120 V60 H150'/><path d='M150 60 H210'/><path d='M210 135 H290'/></g><text x='60' y='128' font-size='12' text-anchor='middle' fill='var(--accent)'>flat</text><text x='120' y='52' font-size='12' text-anchor='middle' fill='var(--accent)'>+ climb</text><text x='160' y='175' font-size='12' text-anchor='middle' fill='currentColor'>fixed time per km and per metre up</text></svg>
pros: Known to most hikers, easy to explain
assumptions: Most routes are climbs and walks on paths, not scrambles

estimates.basis: one formula plus tests on five known routes

options.name: Tobler's hiking function
options.summary: Walking speed changes with slope along every segment, fastest on a gentle downhill.
options.sketch: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 180'><path d='M40 150H290M165 150V25' stroke='currentColor' stroke-opacity='0.6'/><path d='M40 145 C90 140 120 110 150 45 C160 38 170 40 180 55 C210 105 250 138 290 146' fill='none' stroke='var(--accent)' stroke-width='3'/><circle cx='155' cy='42' r='4' fill='var(--accent)'/><text x='60' y='40' font-size='12' fill='currentColor'>speed</text><text x='250' y='168' font-size='12' fill='currentColor'>slope</text><text x='60' y='168' font-size='12' fill='currentColor'>downhill</text><text x='176' y='36' font-size='12' fill='var(--accent)'>fastest</text></svg>
pros: Handles descents as well as climbs
Uses the elevation data the map already has
cons: Needs elevation along the whole route
Harder to explain in one line
assumptions: Elevation data is fine enough to give slope every 50 m or so
risks: Noisy elevation data makes the slope jump and the time too high

estimates.basis: segment the route, smooth elevation, apply the function, test

options.name: Learn from your own tracks
options.summary: Fit a personal pace from the GPS tracks you have already walked.
options.sketch: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 180'><path d='M40 150H290M40 150V25' stroke='currentColor' stroke-opacity='0.6'/><g fill='currentColor' fill-opacity='0.45'><circle cx='70' cy='130' r='3'/><circle cx='95' cy='118' r='3'/><circle cx='110' cy='126' r='3'/><circle cx='140' cy='100' r='3'/><circle cx='160' cy='108' r='3'/><circle cx='185' cy='84' r='3'/><circle cx='210' cy='90' r='3'/><circle cx='235' cy='66' r='3'/><circle cx='260' cy='60' r='3'/></g><path d='M55 138 L275 52' stroke='var(--accent)' stroke-width='3'/><text x='60' y='40' font-size='12' fill='currentColor'>time</text><text x='200' y='168' font-size='12' fill='currentColor'>effort (km and climb)</text><text x='236' y='48' font-size='12' fill='var(--accent)'>your pace</text></svg>
pros: Gets better the more you walk
cons: Nothing to fit for a new user
assumptions: Users have a handful of recorded tracks to import
risks: Tracks with long breaks skew the pace unless breaks are cut out

estimates.basis: track import, break detection, fitting, and a fallback for new users

criteria.name: Easy to explain
criteria.note: A hiker should be able to check the figure in their head.

recommendation: Steep routes are where today's figure goes most wrong, and B fixes that without needing any history. C can come later as a personal adjustment on top of B.

evidence.claim: Naismith's rule allows one hour for every 5 km forward plus one hour for every 600 m of ascent.
Tobler's hiking function gives walking speed as a function of slope, with the highest speed on a slight downhill.
A personal fit needs enough tracks per user to be steadier than a general rule.

change_mind: If the elevation data turns out too coarse for slope every 50 m, A with a descent correction wins on effort.
